Dacia Sandero Will Get an Electric Variant for the First Time, Combustion Models Live On
6 photos
Photo: Dacia
The next-generation Dacia Sandero will have an all-electric variant for the first time. The electric powertrain will borrow parts from the Renault 5 E-Tech, although the Sandero will retain the current platform to accommodate combustion variants. These will include a new entry-level TCe engine and a more affordable full-hybrid powertrain.
European carmakers have been so focused on relaxing emissions regulations that they forgot to take car buyers into consideration. Happy to be allowed to sell combustion vehicles beyond 2035, they failed to notice the tectonic shift that was triggered by the Iran war and the rising fuel prices. As customers flocked to buy electric vehicles, legacy carmakers have few electric models in their lineups.
Dacia has been among the carmakers that were hit the hardest when European customers migrated en masse towards electric vehicles. The budget carmaker has only one electric model in its lineup, the Spring city car . Despite its attractive price and decent performance, the Dacia Spring is far from being able to address all transportation needs of European customers.
Thankfully, the budget carmaker in Renault's portfolio is already working on an electric variant of the Sandero, its most popular model. According to Autocar, the next-generation Dacia Sandero will offer in 2028 an electric powertrain for the first time. Production is scheduled to begin in Morocco in April 2028.
The next-generation Sandero will be fresh, but not entirely new. Autocar reports that Dacia will continue to use the current RGMP platform (previously known as CMF-B). Besides that, the upcoming model will retain the underlying body structure, including the roof, A-pillars, door structures, and glazing.
This has two important benefits. On the one hand, Dacia saves substantially in development costs and tooling at the Casablanca factory in Morocco. Secondly, Dacia can continue to build combustion variants of the Sandero without needing to redesign the platform. The downside is that the Sandero will adapt the RGMP platform to include a battery pack and electric drive unit, with all the negatives.
These crucial parts will be sourced from the Renault 5 E-Tech, including the 44-kWh LFP battery and the 107-hp electric motor. Since these components must be integrated into the ICE platform, expect a few rough edges, especially in terms of packaging and efficiency. The range is expected to hover around 400 km (250 miles), obviously according to the European WLTP standard.
Changes are also expected on the IVCE front. Renault will replace the entry-level 1.0-liter TCe engine with a new 1.2-liter variant still developing 99 hp. A more affordable full-hybrid powertrain is also anticipated, built around a 114-hp 1.2-liter TCe engine.
Even though the platform and bodywork stay largely unchanged, the next-generation Dacia Sandero will feature a complete redesign inspired by the Striker. The dashboard will also be new, with more upscale materials and a more attractive styling. Physical controls will be kept for important functions. Still, the center screen will gain more prominence as the human-machine interface.
